taxonomyRules.multiFacet: A Work may belong to more than one facet; the browse UI should not force one exclusive shelf identity.
taxonomyRules.futureGrowth: As foreign canonical admission expands, language, period, tradition, author and source facets may appear when they have enough real holdings; do not expose them merely because the schema can support them.

coverAudit.currentBatchState: The canonical batch currently records title/author/year/domain but no resolved cover/image/title-page field at Work level.
coverAudit.therefore: Do not pretend that 46 covers already exist. Cover enrichment is a real missing data pass before the visual browse leaf can be implemented faithfully.
resolutionOrder: scanned title page/front matter from the admitted edition when host terms permit
generated editorial representation only as explicit UI fallback
coverAudit.generatedFallbackRule: Generated covers must never be presented as historical covers. They are interface representations derived from canonical metadata.

visual: resolved visual or explicit no-visual state
browseDataMinimum.selection: Always resolves to canonical Work, while the displayed visual may belong to a specific Edition/source.

immediateConsequence: The next visual-design pass should use these six evidence-backed families as the current Chinese browse structure, but should not freeze them as the universal future taxonomy. The first implementation must include a cover/title-page enrichment pipeline rather than filling the page with invented placeholders.
next: Resolve visual/title-page availability for the 46 CLSC canonical Works from their source records/endpoints, while foreign canonical admission runs in parallel; then test the browse leaf with real heterogeneous covers rather than mock cards.
